correctness.rationale: Every element of the nontrivial generalized-dihedral coset is an involution. If such an element shared a cyclic subgroup with a nonidentity kernel element, the two would commute, forcing the kernel element to be an involution; a cyclic group cannot contain two distinct involutions, so every coset element is a leaf adjacent only to the identity. The only kernel leaves are exactly \(T(A)\), so \(At\cup T(A)\) is a false-twin class and forces distinct colors, while the universal identity forces one more. The proposed upper coloring injectively pairs every remaining kernel vertex with a distinct leaf; a nonidentity neighbor of the kernel vertex distinguishes the repeated-color pair. For non-2-groups any involution multiplied by a nontrivial odd-order element lies in a larger cyclic subgroup. For abelian 2-groups, \(T(A)=A[2]\setminus2A\), giving \(2^r-2^s\). The frozen group/graph verifier was read and independently checks twelve cyclic/noncyclic kernels.
correctness.risk: The proof is specific to inversion semidirect products with abelian kernel.

value.rationale: This gives an exact solution of an explicit published graph-invariant problem on a natural infinite group family with arbitrary finite abelian kernel. The answer is structural: isolated involutions are precisely the correction term, and finite abelian 2-group structure converts that obstruction into a closed invariant-factor formula.
value.risk: It does not extend automatically to arbitrary semidirect products or nonabelian kernels.

final_claim: For every nontrivial finite abelian group \(A\), the enhanced power graph of \(\operatorname{Dih}(A)\) has locating chromatic number \(|A|+|T(A)|+1\), where \(T(A)\) consists of kernel involutions contained in no larger cyclic subgroup; this gives \(T(A)=\varnothing\) outside the 2-group case and \(|T(A)|=2^r-2^s\) for \(A\cong\prod_i C_{2^{a_i}}\), with the stated ordinary-dihedral specialization.
limitations: Finite abelian kernels under inversion action only.
No locating-chromatic formula for arbitrary finite groups.
